description: A tracker sequencer: patterns of notes and modulation are typed on its screen and arranged along a timeline, and the rest of the suite puts the result out as voltages

params.text: Plays the whole timeline from its beginning and loops at the end
Plays the selected pattern and loops it; in timeline view it loops the selected instance along with anything else on the same beats
Starts playing again from wherever playback was last stopped
Sets the tempo, 30 to 300 beats per minute
Adds one to the number of lines the cursor moves down after a note or a value is typed
Takes one off the number of lines the cursor moves down after a note or a value is typed
Raises by one the octave that notes typed on the computer keyboard are written at
Lowers by one the octave that notes typed on the computer keyboard are written at
Makes the pattern cursor follow the playhead while the track is playing, so notes can be typed in as it runs
Shows the pattern view, where a pattern's note and CV columns are edited and the track's synths are added and changed
Shows the timeline view, where instances of patterns are placed, stretched and muted along the track
Shows the matrix view, which the maker has not implemented
Shows the tuning view, which draws the current tuning as a circle of one octave
Hides or shows the velocity digits in the pattern's note columns
Hides or shows the panning digits in the pattern's note columns
Hides or shows the delay digits in the pattern's note columns
Hides or shows the glide digits in the pattern's note columns
Hides or shows the effect column in the pattern's note columns

notes: only one Tracker belongs in a patch. The first one added becomes the one the rest of the suite reads, and any further copy does nothing at all.
this module has no jacks. The sound comes out of T-Synth, T-Drum, T-Clock, T-Phase and T-State, and those modules find this one through the plugin rather than through a cable.
the yellow lamp is lit when the module has keyboard focus and a pattern can be typed into, the blue lamp while the track is playing, and the red lamp in record mode.
a pattern is edited with the arrow keys and the digit keys; a note is written by putting the cursor on a pitch and playing a keyboard, and the space bar writes a note stop.
the two screens are single widgets, so nothing drawn on them can be clicked for help. Pattern length and column counts are set by right-clicking the screen itself.
menu: Note effects — lists the letter codes a note's effect column takes, from amplitude and panning randomness to vibrato, tremolo and chance
Shortcuts pattern — lists the keys that edit a pattern
Shortcuts timeline — lists the keys that edit the timeline
Midi — chooses the MIDI device that notes can be played in from
Rate: Sample rate / 1 up to Sample rate / 512 — sets how often the sequencer is stepped, as a division of the engine sample rate; it comes up at a division of 64
Base Pitch — sets the reference frequency the whole track is tuned to, 400Hz to 500Hz
Tuning — holds a slider for each of the twelve notes in cents, along with scale presets and temperament presets such as Pythagorean and Werckmeister III
